text:
**Short answer:** it depends on your trip. For most car or tent camping, a ~288Wh unit is enough. For longer or more power-hungry trips, step up to 1kWh or more.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
These are the ~250-300Wh picks from [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/):
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb): their top pick for light weight and simplicity. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2 (faster recharging, shorter warranty), so check which one you're buying.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W AC): twice the Jackery's AC output, and expandable.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh): built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the version with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC."
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W AC): the budget pick.

Caveat: OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low overall. They suggest the Jackery 300 mainly for phones and laptops. PowerStationGearLab is also affiliate-supported, so treat its rankings with some caution.

## Longer trips, a 12V fridge, or van/overland use
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (under $900 on sale, 39 lb): OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It tested at 1,710Wh usable, and one tester used it for string lights, an electric cooler and device charging. [Review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (under $530 on sale): OutdoorGearLab's best value. It's compact, but the fan is noisy. [Review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** (~$1,079): WIRED's best for camping. It's IP65-rated, drop-resistant, under 40 lb, and has a 5-year warranty. [Review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799): TechRadar's camping pick, and also the van/overland pick at PowerStationGearLab. [Review](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

## A deal I could verify
The **Bluetti AC180** (1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 35 lb, 5-year warranty) is $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF. Dealectric reports testing the code in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. It's a good fit for weekend trips and running tools or small appliances. It has no expansion port, and $499 is the station alone without solar.
**[Buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** (affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you). Confirm the price at checkout.

## Buying notes
- The other review pages link to Amazon and other retailers, but the search results didn't include direct product URLs. Use the review links above to reach current prices, and double-check the exact model name.
- Turn off a CPAP's humidifier to stretch battery life a lot.
- These units are too big to take on planes. Power stations exceed the 100Wh airline limit.
- Black Friday is coming, and TechRadar notes this is a good time to hunt for deals.

If you tell me how many nights you'll camp, what you'll power (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
